The Save America’s Rural Hospitals Act (H.R. 3684) exposes the core problem: Washington’s addiction to temporary fixes over structural reform. While $50B in stabilization funds sounds generous, Manatt Health projects Kansas hospitals alone face $2.65B in Medicaid cuts over a decade—a band-aid on a hemorrhage.

The bill’s Section 401 grants for rural hospital flexibility and Section 106’s wage index adjustments are necessary, but why does every “solution” require new bureaucracy? Rural providers don’t need another slush fund—they need permanent Medicare/Medicaid payment fairness and an end to DC’s budget gimmicks.

Until Congress stops robbing Peter (rural health) to pay Paul (DC pet projects), no amount of “transformation” cash will fix systemic neglect.
